sections.content: If you're searching for real estate deals in Youngstown OH, you've found one of the most investor-friendly markets in the entire Midwest. Low entry prices, strong rental demand, and a steady stream of distressed properties make this former steel city a magnet for wholesalers, flippers, and buy-and-hold investors alike. Whether you're a local pro or an out-of-state investor doing your first deal, Youngstown deserves a serious look. If you're brand new to this, start with our guide on [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) before diving in.
Youngstown OH Real Estate Market Overview

Youngstown sits in Mahoning County in northeast Ohio, about 75 miles southeast of Cleveland and 60 miles northwest of Pittsburgh. The city experienced a dramatic population decline after the steel industry collapsed in the late 1970s and 1980s, dropping from a peak of 170,000 residents to roughly 60,000 today. That demographic shift created one of the largest inventories of cheap, distressed housing in the country — and that's exactly what savvy real estate investors look for.

The median home price in Youngstown hovers between $45,000 and $65,000, making it one of the most affordable markets in the United States. Comparable single-family homes that would cost $250,000 in Columbus or $400,000 in Columbus suburbs sell here for $30,000 to $80,000. That extreme affordability is the foundation of every profitable strategy available in this market. You can explore current listings, deal flow, and market data specifically for this city at [AIWholesail's Youngstown market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/youngstown-oh).
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Youngstown

Not every zip code in Youngstown is created equal. Investors need to understand the micro-markets within the city to avoid problem areas and target the spots where rents are stable and buyer demand exists.
Top Investor-Friendly Areas

items: Boardman Township (44512): Just south of the city limits, Boardman is the strongest submarket in the area. Median home prices range from $90,000 to $150,000. Lower vacancy, better school ratings, and stable blue-collar rental demand make this the go-to for buy-and-hold investors.

Canfield / Poland Township: These suburban areas offer slightly higher price points ($120,000–$180,000) but attract tenants with stronger income and lower turnover. Great for landlords who want lower management headaches.

Youngstown's North Side (44505): One of the city's more stabilized neighborhoods. You can find distressed properties here in the $15,000–$40,000 range that rent for $600–$800/month after rehab, producing strong cash-on-cash returns.

Struthers and Campbell: Small working-class suburbs bordering Youngstown proper. Home prices in the $50,000–$90,000 range and consistent rental demand from manufacturing workers make these solid value-add targets.
Liberty Township (44505 / 44506 border area): A transitional market offering deep-discount wholesale deals alongside legitimate rental upside for investors willing to manage at a distance.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Drive the neighborhood (or use Google Street View if you're out of state) before committing to any deal in Youngstown. Block-by-block conditions vary dramatically. A street with three boarded-up houses isn't necessarily a deal-killer — but it does mean your exit strategy needs to be bulletproof.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Youngstown
Wholesale Deals

Youngstown is a wholesaler's dream. The city has a massive inventory of vacant, tax-delinquent, and probate properties. It's common to find motivated sellers willing to part with properties for $5,000 to $20,000, which wholesalers can then assign to cash buyers for a $3,000 to $10,000 assignment fee. The key is building a reliable cash buyer list of local rehabbers and landlords who understand the market. If you're new to this strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks you through the entire process step by step. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is especially valuable here since many of Youngstown's best properties never hit the MLS.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Flipping in Youngstown requires discipline because your ARV ceiling is relatively low. A fully renovated 3-bedroom home in Boardman might sell for $120,000 to $145,000, while the same house in Youngstown proper might top out at $60,000 to $80,000. Successful flippers here work in volume, targeting properties they can acquire for $10,000 to $25,000, rehab for $25,000 to $40,000, and resell for $70,000 to $100,000. Margins can be strong — $15,000 to $30,000 per deal — but you need accurate ARV estimates before you commit. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to run your numbers before making an offer.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

This is where Youngstown truly shines for long-term wealth building. A renovated 3-bedroom home in a solid part of Boardman or Struthers can be purchased for $60,000 to $85,000 and rented for $850 to $1,100 per month. That's a gross rent multiplier of 7–9x, which produces cash-on-cash returns in the 12% to 20% range for all-cash buyers — numbers that are nearly impossible to find in major metros. Section 8 vouchers are widely used in Mahoning County, which can mean guaranteed monthly rent deposits directly from the housing authority.

"The best real estate investors aren't chasing hot markets — they're finding cold markets with real fundamentals. Youngstown has low prices, steady rental demand, and motivated sellers. That's the formula."
Local Market Trends to Watch in 2024–2025

items: Rising rent demand: As affordability tightens nationally, more renters are relocating to low-cost metros like Youngstown. Vacancy rates in Boardman and Struthers have trended downward over the past two years.

Investor competition is increasing: Word is out. More out-of-state investors are targeting Youngstown, which means the best wholesale deals move faster than they did five years ago. Speed and relationships matter more than ever.

Land bank activity: Mahoning County Land Bank actively acquires and resells tax-delinquent properties. Investors can purchase properties directly through the land bank, sometimes at prices under $5,000 with clear title — a major advantage.
Rehab cost pressure: Labor and material costs have risen in northeast Ohio like everywhere else. Budget $25 to $45 per square foot for moderate rehabs and $50 to $70 for full gut renovations.

Population stabilization: Youngstown's population decline has slowed significantly, and small business investment is beginning to return to the downtown corridor. This is a positive long-term signal for property values.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Investing in Youngstown from outside Ohio is absolutely viable, but it requires a different approach than buying in your home market. Remote investing in this market comes with unique advantages (low prices, strong cash flow) and unique risks (deferred maintenance, property management challenges, tenant screening). Here's how to do it right.

items: Build a local team first: Before you buy anything, find a reliable property manager, a contractor who works in the specific zip codes you're targeting, and a local real estate attorney. This team is everything.

Inspect every property in person or hire an independent inspector: Photos are deceptive in this market. A house that looks cosmetically rough may have a solid foundation; a house that looks clean may have serious structural or environmental issues.

Use the Mahoning County Auditor's website: This free resource shows ownership records, tax delinquency status, and sale history for every parcel in the county. It's one of the best deal-sourcing tools available.

Run every deal through a deal analyzer before making an offer: Don't rely on gut feel. Use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to stress-test your numbers against multiple exit strategies.

Start with Boardman or Struthers: These submarkets are lower risk for out-of-state investors because property values are more stable, tenant quality is higher, and resale demand is stronger than in Youngstown proper.

Network with local wholesalers: The best off-market deals in Youngstown are passed through local networks before they ever hit any list. Attend local REIA meetings (the Mahoning Valley REIA is active) or connect with local wholesalers online.

Understand how to analyze deals at a deep level: Knowing how to read a deal correctly is the single most important skill. Our guide on [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) will help you avoid costly mistakes.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When evaluating rental properties in Youngstown, use a 45–50% expense ratio (not the common 40% rule) to account for higher vacancy and maintenance costs in this market. Being conservative with your projections protects your cash flow when reality hits.
Is Youngstown Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Youngstown is not a market for investors chasing appreciation. Home values here are unlikely to double in five years the way they might in a high-growth Sun Belt city. What Youngstown offers instead is immediate cash flow, deep-discount entry points, and a consistent deal pipeline for wholesalers. If your goal is to build monthly passive income or to practice the fundamentals of real estate investing without risking huge capital, this market is hard to beat. The investors who struggle here are those who underestimate rehab costs, overestimate ARVs, or buy in the wrong neighborhoods without local guidance.
